[ADVOCATE NAME], Advocate
[CHAMBERS ADDRESS] | Email: [EMAIL] | Tel: [PHONE] | Enrolment No. [ENROLMENT NO.]

Ref. No.: [REF]/2026                                                    Date: [DATE OF NOTICE]
BY REGISTERED POST A.D. AND BY EMAIL AT [NOTICEE EMAIL ADDRESS]

To,
XYZ Developers LLP,
a Limited Liability Partnership incorporated under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, having its registered office at [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS OF XYZ DEVELOPERS LLP], acting through its designated partner(s)/authorised signatory.

Sub: Legal notice for recovery of Rs. 70,00,000/- (Rupees Seventy Lakh only) towards outstanding certified dues under the Construction Agreement dated 15 February 2026, together with contractual interest at 12% (twelve percent) per annum and damages, and invocation of the arbitration clause contained in the said Agreement.

1. That my Client, ABC Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd., is a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, having its registered office at [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS OF ABC INFRASTRUCTURE PVT. LTD.], and is engaged in the business of construction and infrastructure development.

2. That you, XYZ Developers LLP, are a limited liability partnership engaged in real estate development, having your registered office at the address stated above.

3. That by a Construction Agreement dated 15 February 2026 executed between my Client and you (hereinafter "the said Agreement"), my Client was engaged to carry out construction works for the project situated at [PROJECT ADDRESS] for a total consideration of Rs. 2,80,00,000/- (Rupees Two Crore Eighty Lakh only), on the terms and conditions recorded therein.

4. That my Client duly mobilised resources and commenced execution of the works in terms of the said Agreement and, as on date, has completed approximately 90% (ninety percent) of the contracted scope of work, which progress and quality of work has not been disputed by you at any stage.

5. That the work executed by my Client stands duly certified by the project engineer appointed under the said Agreement, being [NAME/DESIGNATION OF PROJECT ENGINEER], vide certificate(s) dated [DATE(S) OF CERTIFICATION], confirming the value of work done and the amount payable to my Client.

6. That despite such certification, you have failed and neglected to release payment, and a sum of Rs. 70,00,000/- (Rupees Seventy Lakh only) remains outstanding and unpaid to my Client as on date.

7. That my Client, through its authorised representatives, addressed multiple reminders to you by email on [DATES OF EMAIL REMINDERS], calling upon you to clear the outstanding dues, to none of which you have responded or offered any explanation for the non-payment.

8. That my Client has, in the past few days, learnt that you have proceeded to engage another contractor, namely [NAME OF SUBSTITUTE CONTRACTOR, IF KNOWN], for the balance/remaining works under the project, without having terminated the said Agreement with my Client in accordance with its terms, and without settling my Client's outstanding dues, which conduct is asserted by my Client to be in bad faith and in derogation of your obligations under the said Agreement.

9. That the cause of action for this notice arose, in the first instance, on the date of certification of the work by the project engineer when the payment became due, and arose further and continued on each date on which your non-payment persisted despite reminders, and arose finally on the date my Client learnt of your engagement of a substitute contractor without termination of the said Agreement, and continues to subsist as on date.

That your failure to release payment against duly certified work constitutes a breach of the payment obligations under Clause [NUMBER OF PAYMENT CLAUSE] of the said Agreement. That your act of engaging a substitute contractor for the balance works, without terminating the said Agreement in the manner and upon the notice period prescribed therein, further constitutes a breach of Clause [NUMBER OF TERMINATION CLAUSE] of the said Agreement and amounts to a repudiation of your obligations towards my Client. In consequence of the above breaches, my Client is entitled to (i) the outstanding principal amount of Rs. 70,00,000/- (Rupees Seventy Lakh only); (ii) contractual interest thereon at 12% (twelve percent) per annum as stipulated in Clause [NUMBER OF INTEREST CLAUSE] of the said Agreement, from the respective due dates of certification till the date of actual payment; and (iii) damages under Sections 73 and 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 for the loss and injury occasioned to my Client by reason of your breach, including loss of business opportunity and displacement from the project, the quantum whereof is being independently assessed and is expressly reserved for claim in the arbitral proceedings invoked hereunder.

You are hereby called upon to preserve all records, books of account, correspondence, measurement books, site registers, certificates issued by the project engineer, minutes of meetings, and all electronic communications including emails and messages, relating to the said Agreement and the works executed thereunder, including any communications and agreements with the substitute contractor engaged by you. You are directed not to destroy, alter, tamper with or part with possession of any such record or communication. An adverse inference shall be liable to be drawn against you, and appropriate orders sought before the competent forum, in the event of any spoliation of such evidence.

That the said Agreement contains an arbitration clause, being Clause [NUMBER OF ARBITRATION CLAUSE] thereof, providing for reference of disputes between the parties to arbitration. My Client hereby unconditionally and unequivocally invokes the said arbitration clause under Section 21 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, and this notice shall constitute a notice of invocation of arbitration for all purposes under the said Act. My Client proposes the name of [PROPOSED ARBITRATOR NAME, IF ANY, OR STATE PROCEDURE UNDER THE CLAUSE] to act as the sole arbitrator / to constitute the arbitral tribunal in terms of Clause [NUMBER] of the said Agreement, and calls upon you to communicate your concurrence to the said appointment, or to make your own nomination in terms of the said clause, within 15 (fifteen) days of receipt of this notice, failing which my Client shall be constrained to approach the competent court for appointment of an arbitrator in accordance with law.

TAKE NOTICE that in the event of your failure to comply with the demands made herein within the period stipulated above, my Client shall be constrained to proceed with the arbitral reference already invoked herein, including by approaching the competent court for appointment of an arbitrator, and to claim the outstanding principal, contractual interest, damages, and costs therein, entirely at your risk as to costs and consequences. My Client expressly reserves all rights and remedies available to it in law and in equity, including the right to seek interim measures of protection, without prejudice to any other right or remedy available to my Client under the said Agreement or in law.

Yours faithfully,

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Advocate
Counsel for ABC Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd.

(A copy of this notice is retained in my office for further necessary action.)

assumptions.assumption: Registered office addresses of both ABC Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. and XYZ Developers LLP
assumptions.why: Not supplied in facts; required to identify parties in the notice

assumptions.assumption: The project engineer's name/designation and the certification date(s)
assumptions.why: Facts state certification occurred but do not name the engineer or the date(s) of certification

assumptions.assumption: Specific clause numbers for payment, termination, interest, and arbitration in the Construction Agreement
assumptions.why: Facts confirm these clauses exist (interest at 12% and an arbitration clause) but do not supply clause numbers

assumptions.assumption: Dates of the email reminders sent by the client
assumptions.why: Facts state multiple reminders were sent by email but do not specify dates

assumptions.assumption: Name of the substitute/new contractor engaged by XYZ Developers LLP, if known to the client
assumptions.why: Facts state a new contractor was engaged but do not name them

assumptions.assumption: Cost of notice quantified at Rs. 25,000/-
assumptions.why: No figure was supplied by the client for the cost of the notice; a conventional placeholder figure was used

assumptions.assumption: Proposed arbitrator's name or the appointment procedure under the arbitration clause
assumptions.why: Facts confirm an arbitration clause exists but do not state its mechanism (sole arbitrator, three-member panel, appointing authority, etc.)

assumptions.assumption: Project/site address is distinct from the registered office addresses
assumptions.why: A construction contract ordinarily specifies a project site; not supplied in facts

drafting_notes.issue: Arbitration invoked under s.21 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 in unconditional terms, as required. However, the notice also refers to 'arbitral proceedings' as the exclusive contemplated remedy in the TAKE NOTICE clause to avoid the conflict between invoking arbitration and simultaneously threatening a civil suit, since a valid arbitration clause ordinarily bars a suit under s.8 of the 1996 Act.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Confirm the arbitration clause is valid, wide enough to cover this dispute (payment and termination issues), and does not carve out an exception permitting a civil suit for recovery; if it does, the TAKE NOTICE clause should be revised accordingly.

drafting_notes.issue: Clause numbers for payment, termination, interest and arbitration provisions have not been supplied and are marked as placeholders
drafting_notes.recommendation: Obtain a copy of the executed Construction Agreement dated 15 February 2026 and insert the correct clause numbers before issuance; an incorrect or missing clause reference weakens the breach allegation.

drafting_notes.issue: Damages under Sections 73 and 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 have been claimed but not quantified
drafting_notes.recommendation: Instruct client to prepare a computation of loss (e.g., loss of profit on displaced 10% balance work, mobilisation costs, idle resource costs) before the statement of claim is filed in arbitration, since unquantified damages claims are open to challenge.

drafting_notes.issue: The proposed arbitrator/appointment mechanism has been left as a placeholder since the arbitration clause's exact mechanism (sole arbitrator, panel, institutional rules) was not provided
drafting_notes.recommendation: Retrieve the exact text of the arbitration clause before despatch; if it names an appointing authority or institution, the notice must follow that mechanism precisely to avoid a defective s.21 invocation.

drafting_notes.issue: Allegation regarding engagement of a substitute contractor without termination is based on facts asserted by the client and is not documented
drafting_notes.recommendation: Ask client whether this is based on direct knowledge, a site report, or hearsay, and obtain any supporting communication or evidence (e.g., site photographs, new contractor's presence, correspondence) before relying on it in arbitral pleadings.

drafting_notes.issue: No mention of a specific termination clause number or notice period for termination that XYZ Developers LLP may be said to have bypassed
drafting_notes.recommendation: Verify the termination clause's notice period and procedure in the Agreement; this strengthens the breach argument regarding engagement of a new contractor without proper termination.

drafting_notes.issue: Interest claimed strictly as per the contractual rate of 12% per annum under the Agreement, and not under the Interest Act, 1978, since a contractual rate is asserted to exist and takes precedence
drafting_notes.recommendation: Confirm from the Agreement that Clause [NUMBER] indeed stipulates 12% per annum on delayed payments, as stated in client instructions, and that this rate is not restricted to a specific category of delay only.

drafting_notes.issue: The user's instruction to include 'chronology of facts' and 'detailed legal notice' has been complied with by numbering the recitals chronologically from the Agreement date through to the engagement of the substitute contractor
drafting_notes.recommendation: No further action needed; instructing advocate should verify chronology once actual certification and reminder dates are supplied.
